## What to Build

`cmd/partio/status.go` calls `mgr.CleanupStale()` inside `runStatus`, which transitions any stale active or idle session to the `ended` state — writing to `current.json` — as a side effect of a command the user runs to inspect state. Running `partio status` can silently change the session record the user is trying to read.

The fix is to move the `CleanupStale` call out of `runStatus` and instead surface a stale-session indicator in the status output. Cleanup belongs with `partio doctor`, which already owns remediation of unhealthy state.

Specifically:
- Remove lines 52–57 of `cmd/partio/status.go` (the `mgr.CleanupStale(...)` call and its result handling).
- Read the current session from the manager without mutating it: replace the cleanup call with `mgr.Current()`.
- If the session is active or idle but its state file is older than `cfg.StaleSessionThreshold`, print `Session:    stale (run 'partio doctor' to clean up)` rather than silently advancing the state to ended.
- If no session exists, print nothing or `Session:    none`.
- `partio doctor` already handles remediation; its cleanup call is unchanged.

## Why This Matters

`partio status` is a read-only inspection command. A developer who runs it to check whether an agent session is being tracked should not find that the act of checking has already ended the session. The mutation is invisible: the INFO log line (line 55–56) goes to the log sink, not stdout, so the user sees `Status: enabled` with no indication that anything changed. If the same session would have been picked up by the next commit's post-commit hook (because it was not yet ended), that commit now finds no active session and creates no checkpoint.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `partio status` does not write to session state files under any code path (no calls to `CleanupStale`, `MarkCondensed`, or `Clear` in `runStatus`)
- [ ] When a session state file exists and is stale (age > threshold, process gone), `partio status` prints a stale indicator and does not modify the file
- [ ] When a session state file exists and is healthy, `partio status` prints its state unchanged
- [ ] `partio doctor` continues to clean up stale sessions via its existing `CleanupStale` call
- [ ] `make test` passes
- [ ] `make lint` passes

## Premise

<!-- partio:premise:v1 -->

- `runStatus` in `cmd/partio/status.go` calls `mgr.CleanupStale()`, which transitions a stale active or idle session to ended by writing to the session state file [evidence: `cmd/partio/status.go`]

## Gathered Evidence

**Claim — `runStatus` calls `mgr.CleanupStale()`**
Evidence: `cmd/partio/status.go`
Verdict: `holds`
Excerpt: lines 52–57 —
```go
mgr := session.NewManager(partioDir)
if result, err := mgr.CleanupStale(cfg.StaleSessionThreshold.Duration()); err != nil {
    slog.Debug("stale session cleanup failed", "error", err)
} else if result.Cleaned {
    slog.Info("stale session cleaned up", "id", result.Session.ID)
}
```
`CleanupStale` (`internal/session/cleanup.go:25`) transitions the session to `StateEnded` and calls `m.save(s)` which writes `current.json`. A read-only status command is producing a durable state mutation.
